validity.recommendation: no action — existence, diameter, and non-duplicate status all corroborated
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, independent of gem.wiki. This is the real, distinct 'Torzhok–Dolina' trunk (Russia→Belarus→Ukraine), NOT gem.wiki-only. Sources spanning 20 years: East European Gas Analysis (eegas.com/belarus1.htm, 2006/2014) lists it by name as a separate line from the parallel 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi' (3x1220mm) and 'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina' (2x1220mm) systems, giving it 1420mm (56-in) diameter; RBC Ukraine (2006) reports a Ukraine-Belarus government agreement specifically on the 'operating procedure for the Torzhok-Dolina and Ivatsevichi-Dolina pipelines' (two named, distinct systems); Vesti.ru (Russian state media, Nov 8 2014) reported a pipe rupture on the 'Torzhok-Dolina' line in Torzhok district, Tver Oblast; ngsrb.com (a Russian pipeline-construction contractor) documents a 2016-08-01 to 2017-07-31 capital-repair project on a 48.772 km section of MG 'Torzhok – Dolina', 1420mm diameter, near Torzhok; Ukrainian Wikipedia (uk.wikipedia.org, real Wikipedia, not gem.wiki) carries a dedicated, well-footnoted article with construction history (below). DIAMETER 1420mm: independently confirmed by eegas.com AND isans.org (existing sheet ref, already verified: 'Torzhok — Dolina diametrom 1420 mm' — both explicit, tier=high. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: NOT the same physical pipe as P3484/P5938 ('Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna', 1220mm, 292km) despite the shared 'Dolyna' hub — every source above (eegas, isans, rbc.ua, uk.wikipedia) treats 'Torzhok-Dolina' (1420mm, single thread, via Smolensk/Mazyr) and 'Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi'+'Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina' (1220mm, multi-thread, via Minsk) as two SEPARATE, parallel corridors feeding the same Dolyna hub from different routes — confirmed not-a-duplicate. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both correctly recorded for this large-diameter international trunk — no concern. NAMING: the GEM title adds 'Smolensk-Mazyr' as explicit waypoints not named in eegas/isans (which just say 'Torzhok-Dolina'), but uk.wikipedia independently confirms Mazyr (Mozyr) IS on the route — the Mozyr underground gas storage facility in Belarus sits on this pipeline (category tag 'Мозир' on the wiki article) — so the fuller GEM name is plausible/supported, not fabricated. LENGTH 1300km: no source gives a single end-to-end figure (uk.wikipedia only gives the Ukraine-territory portion, 529 km); a geographic sanity check (Torzhok→Smolensk→Mazyr→Dolyna waypoint routing, great-circle sum ~1090 km + typical 15-20% pipeline-routing overhead) lands in the 1250-1300 km range, so 1300 km is plausible and uncontradicted, but remains uncorroborated by a citable numeric source — leave as-is, tier=low/unresolved rather than a hard concern.

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity=22 bcm/y and Status=operating for Update review — verify current cross-border throughput, don't just re-confirm nameplate diameter
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: GEM's 22.00 bcm/y matches isans.org's stated figure exactly (already the sheet's own working ref: 'gazoprovod «Torzhok — Dolina» diametrom 1420 mm (okolo 22 mlrd kub.m. v god)' — tier=medium as a single source, since I could not independently corroborate the 22 bcm figure a second time (belarus-tr.gazprom.ru and btg.by, both cited by gem.wiki for this row, are geo-blocked/unreachable from here — ConnectTimeout, consistent with the sheet's own existing_ref_checks). BUT this 22 bcm/y reads as a NAMEPLATE/diameter-implied design figure, not achieved throughput: Ukrainian Wikipedia's well-footnoted article states the pipe's linear section (incl. 529 km through Ukraine) was completed by 1995-1996 WITHOUT compressor stations, so the as-built system capacity was only ~6 bcm/y — not the ~22 bcm/y the 1420mm diameter would imply with full compression — and Ukraine repeatedly proposed finishing the 4 compressor stations needed on its territory in the early 2000s, but Russia chose pipeline routes bypassing Ukraine instead, so it was never completed. As of 2007 (the most recent figure the source gives) actual throughput was only 1.5-2.7 bcm/y — roughly one-tenth of the recorded Capacity value. STATUS: Status=operating needs a fresh look, not a rubber stamp. This line's documented purpose is carrying Russian-origin gas from Torzhok across Belarus INTO Ukraine at Dolyna. Ukraine has made zero direct purchases of Russian gas since 25 Nov 2015 (well-established, near-universally reported Ukrainian gas-sector fact, confirmed independently of this pipeline) — which, given the line's stated function, implies the cross-border (Belarus→Ukraine) flow direction has likely been dormant for roughly a decade, on top of the pre-existing compressor-station shortfall. I found no DATED source describing this specific line's status after 2007 (the ngsrb.com repair project, 2016-17, is on the RUSSIAN section near Torzhok itself and doesn't tell us about the cross-border flow), so per the country brief I'm not asserting a status change on general-transit grounds alone — but this is exactly the kind of row that deserves a targeted follow-up: does the pipe still carry any gas across into Ukraine today (e.g. reverse/local use, feeding the Mozyr UGS in Belarus without crossing the border), or has the Ukrainian portion effectively been idle since 2015-2022 despite still being 'physically operating' pipe.

validity.recommendation: add Ukraine's Gas TSO (tsoua.com) as a co-operator for the Ukrainian segment; the current single Operator value is incomplete for a cross-border trunk
validity.researcher_notes: Operator is recorded as ONLY 'Gazprom Transgaz Belarus JSC' for a pipeline whose own StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea are Russia→Ukraine (transiting Belarus). Per the country's core operatorship fact: Gazprom does not own or operate any section of Ukraine's gas transmission system — since 1 Jan 2020 that is the Gas TSO of Ukraine (tsoua.com). Owner1/Owner2 already correctly split this ('Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' + 'Gazprom PJSC'), but Operator names only the Belarusian transit operator and omits both the Ukrainian TSO (for the 529 km Ukrainian segment) and any Russian-side operator (for the Torzhok-to-border segment in Tver/Smolensk Oblasts). Could not verify a specific ref for this in this pass — tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/ 403'd and the Belarusian operator sources (btg.by, belarus-tr.gazprom.ru) are geo/connect-blocked from here, matching the sheet's own existing_ref_checks — so no new ref proposed; flagging for Update to add the Ukrainian TSO as a co-operator with a properly sourced ref.

fills.researcher_notes: eegas.com's Belarus pipeline map/list names 'Torzhok-Dolina, 1420 mm (56-in)' as a discrete Russia→Belarus→Ukraine trunk (distinguishing it from the parallel Torzhok-Minsk-Ivatsevichi and Ivatsevichi-Kobrin-Dolina systems); uk.wikipedia.org's dedicated, footnoted article gives explicit endpoint coordinates for both Torzhok (57°2'13"N 34°57'0"E, Tver Oblast, Russia) and Dolyna (48°58'51"N 24°0'9"E, Ukraine), and categorizes the pipeline under 'Газопроводи Росії', 'Газопроводи Білорусі' and 'Газопроводи України'. Two independent sources agreeing on both endpoints and both countries — tier=high.

summary: P0779 (Torzhok-Dolina) is a real, well-documented Russia→Belarus→Ukraine trunk, independently confirmed via eegas.com/rbc.ua/vesti.ru/ngsrb.com/uk.wikipedia and clearly distinct from the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna line (P3484/P5938) — not a duplicate. Diameter (1420mm) and non-duplicate status confirmed high tier; Location filled (high tier, 2 sources). Two open concerns staged: (1) spec/status — Capacity=22 bcm/y looks like nameplate/diameter-implied design capacity rather than achieved throughput (uk.wikipedia: no compressor stations were ever built, so as-built capacity was only ~6 bcm/y and actual 2007 throughput just 1.5-2.7 bcm/y; combined with Ukraine's documented zero direct Russian-gas purchases since Nov 2015, the cross-border Status=operating deserves a dedicated follow-up, though no post-2007 dated source on this specific line was found); (2) attribution — Operator names only the Belarusian transit operator, omitting Ukraine's Gas TSO for the Ukrainian segment. Length (1300km) is geographically plausible but UNRESOLVED (no independent numeric source found).
